differences.writeup_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed one stance direction lifts association pass@10 sharply. We hypothesised that an independently written contrast would capture the same direction (cosine 0.89–0.91 at L20–24) and that averaging the two would denoise the stance estimate.
differences.what: the write-up names the prior paper (Raman et al. 2026 / white-bear steering) as the source whose single-direction finding motivated the method, and frames the fused-direction result as an extension of/built on that finding; the message never mentions this paper at all, describing the fused-direction result as a self-contained finding.

rationale: The write-up explicitly credits Raman et al. (2026) as having shown that one stance direction lifts pass@10 sharply, and frames the fused two-direction approach as a hypothesis-driven extension of that prior result, ending with a claim of a 'new finding' relative to that baseline. The closing message describes the same mechanics (two stance directions, cosine similarity, fused vector, pass@10 results) but never mentions Raman et al. (2026) or any prior paper, presenting the ensemble-averaging result as an unqualified demonstration without acknowledging the source paper's groundwork.
